name: Debir
overview: Debir was a male king who ruled over the city of Eglon during the Israelite conquest of the land, as recorded in Joshua 10:3. His role as a king places him among the local rulers opposing Israel's advance. Scripture identifies him specifically as the King of Eglon, though no tribal affiliation is given.
namesAndTitles: The name 'Debir' means 'back room,' referring to the inner chamber of a shrine or temple used for oracle pronouncements. This proper name is not indicated as given by God. Additionally, his title 'King of Eglon' directly identifies his political role and territorial domain.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record any family relationships for Debir beyond his position as King of Eglon. There are no further relational details provided in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Debir's significance lies in his opposition to Israel during the conquest of Canaan. As King of Eglon, he represents one of the local rulers who allied against Israel, highlighting the resistance faced by God's people as they took possession of the Promised Land. His mention in Joshua 10:3 situates him within the broader narrative of God's fulfillment of His promises through Israel's military campaigns.
